mainTopic: Holy scrolls bought from or written by a גוי or a מין, and the משנה on not remarrying a wife divorced for a שם רע or a נדר
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה: we may not buy ספרים, תפילין and מזוזות from גוים for more than their value, because of תיקון העולם. רב בודיא suggests this proves that a ספר תורה found with a גוי may be read from, but רב אשי answers that we may buy it only to put it away. רב נחמן then gives a tradition sorting ספרי תורה written by, or found with, a מין or a גוי into ones that are burned, put away, or read from. The גמרא sees three ברייתות clash over a scroll written by a גוי. It explains that each follows a different תנא: רבי אליעזר, רב המנונא's ברייתא, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It then shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's case in צידן involved a גר who hid his Judaism out of fear. Next, a ברייתא allows paying up to an איסתירא above value, and a story about אביי shows the danger of offering too little. A new משנה follows: a man who divorces his wife because of a שם רע or a נדר may not remarry her, with views from רבי יהודה, רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר, and a story from צידן. The גמרא begins with רב נחמן's condition that the husband must state his reason, and this discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the משנה: for the betterment of the world
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the משנה give the reason for its rule: תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the משנה. They explain why we may not pay more than the real value for holy items held by גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that we do not buy ספרים, תפילין and מזוזות from גוים for more than they are worth. The reason is תיקון העולם: if we overpay, thieves will steal more holy items to sell back to us. The גמרא is about to build on this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Betterment of the world: a rule made for the good of society
The core teaching the גמרא discusses

phrases.english: Because of the betterment of the world.
phrases.notes: This finishes the משנה's rule: don't overpay a גוי for ספרים, תפילין or מזוזות, so people won't steal them to sell.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closing reason of the משנה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We may not overpay for holy items held by גוים, because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: רב בודיא infers that a ספר תורה found with a גוי may be read
steps.stepSummary: רב בודיא reads the משנה closely: only overpaying is forbidden, so buying at value is allowed. Doesn't that show a ספר תורה found with a גוי is fit for reading?
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רב בודיא said to רב אשי: It is only for more than their value that we may not buy them. But for their value, we do buy them. Can we learn from this that a ספר תורה found in the hands of a גוי may be read from?
steps.whatsHappening: רב בודיא makes an inference from the wording of the משנה. Since buying at the normal price is allowed, he suggests the ספר תורה must be usable for reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only forbids paying too much, which implies paying a fair price is fine. Why buy it unless we can use it? So רב בודיא proposes that a ספר תורה found with a גוי is kosher to read from. We are not worried that the גוי himself wrote it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
Their actual value, their fair price
Learn from this: a formula for drawing a proof
We may read from it (in public, as a kosher ספר תורה)

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב בּוּדְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Budya said to Rav Ashi:
It is for more than their value
that we may not buy them,
but for their value, we do buy them;
can we learn from this that a Torah scroll
that is found in the hands of a gentile may be read from?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּמְצָא בְּיַד גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implied ruling out of the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: A ספר תורה found with a גוי is kosher for reading.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's implication that buying at fair value is allowed.

steps.title: רב אשי: maybe we buy it only to put it away
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that buying it does not prove it is fit to read. We may buy it just to bury it respectfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is bought in order to put it away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רב בודיא's proof. The purchase could be only to save the scroll from disrespect and then put it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב בודיא assumed we buy the scroll in order to use it. רב אשי shows another reason to buy it: so it is not mistreated by the גוי, and then we do גניזה. So the משנה tells us nothing about whether the scroll is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps: often opens a rejection of a proof
To put away (bury or store) a holy item that can't be used

steps.confusionAlert: Buying the scroll does not mean we will use it. Holy texts that can't be used still need respectful burial, so rescuing them is worth money too.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is to put it away.
phrases.notes: This is רב אשי's answer to רב בודיא, even though the גמרא doesn't say his name again.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא לִגְנוֹז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The משנה no longer settles whether such a scroll may be read; רב נחמן's tradition in the next step addresses it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed buying means using. Buying could be for גניזה.

steps.title: רב נחמן's tradition on ספרי תורה of a מין and a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a received rule. A scroll written by a מין is burned. One written by a גוי is put away. One found with a מין is put away. One found with a גוי is disputed: put away or read.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We have a tradition. A ספר תורה written by a מין is burned. One written by a גוי is put away. One found in the hands of a מין is put away. One found in the hands of a גוי: some say it is put away, and some say we may read from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a clear list of rulings for ספרי תורה, based on who wrote them or who had them. This touches exactly on רב בודיא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מין's own writing is burned, likely because we fear he wrote it for idolatry, so it has no holiness. A גוי's writing is not kosher but still put away. When we only know where the scroll was found, a מין is treated strictly, while for a גוי there are two opinions. So רב בודיא's question is really a known dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a tradition
A heretic: a Jew who left the faith and serves idols
Some say: introduces two versions of a ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Written by a מין: burn. Written by a גוי: put away. Found with a מין: put away. Found with a גוי: a dispute between putting away and reading.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: We have a tradition:
A Torah scroll that a heretic wrote should be burned;
if a gentile wrote it, it should be put away.
If it was found in the hands of a heretic, it should be put away.
If it was found in the hands of a gentile,
some say it should be put away,
and some say we may read from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, נָקְטִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a tradition that addresses the question left open in steps 2-3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Written by a מין: burned. Written by a גוי: put away. Found with a מין: put away. Found with a גוי: disputed between putting away and reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the base the rest of the sugya works with, starting with the ברייתות in the next step.

steps.title: Three ברייתות clash over a ספר תורה written by a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings three ברייתות about a ספר תורה written by a גוי. One says burn it, one says put it away, and one says read from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ספר תורה written by a גוי: one ברייתא teaches it should be burned. Another teaches it should be put away. Another teaches we may read from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a three-way contradiction between ברייתות about a scroll written by a גוי. It is setting up a resolution that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said a scroll written by a גוי is put away. But the ברייתות give all three possible rulings. The גמרא now needs to explain how they fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in another ברייתא
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: A Torah scroll that a gentile wrote:
one teaching says: it should be burned,
and another teaching says: it should be put away,
and another teaching says: we may read from it!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: יִשָּׂרֵף, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: יִגָּנֵז, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: קוֹרִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a contradiction among ברייתות on the same case רב נחמן ruled on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling for a ספר תורה written by a גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three ברייתות give three different rulings on the same case: burn, put away, read.

steps.title: The 'burn it' ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that says to burn a scroll written by a גוי follows רבי אליעזר. He holds that a גוי's plain intent is for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. The ברייתא that says 'burn it' is רבי אליעזר, who says that a גוי's unspecified intent is for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the contradiction between the three ברייתות. It explains the first one: 'burn it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three ברייתות do not really contradict each other. They come from different תנאים. רבי אליעזר assumes a גוי writes with idolatrous intent, so the scroll is treated like one written by a מין, and it is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening of an answer

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
That which is taught, 'it should be burned'
is רבי אליעזר,
who says:
The unspecified intention of a gentile is for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins resolving the contradiction raised in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The three ברייתות seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Burn it' follows רבי אליעזר, who assumes a גוי writes for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The 'put it away' ברייתא follows רב המנונא's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that says to put the scroll away follows רב המנונא's ברייתא. It says only someone included in tying תפילין may write holy texts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא that says 'put it away' follows the ברייתא taught by רב המנונא son of רבא from פשרוניא. It says that a ספר תורה, תפילין, or מזוזות written by a מין, a מסור, a גוי, a slave, a woman, a minor, a כותי, or a Jewish apostate are unfit. The verse says 'tie them' and 'write them,' so whoever is included in tying is included in writing, and whoever is not, is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second ברייתא, 'put it away.' It shows which תנא holds that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא's ברייתא lists the גוי together with others who cannot write holy texts. The verse links tying תפילין to writing, so only someone obligated in תפילין can write. The scroll is not holy enough to read from, but it is not idolatrous either, so it is put away rather than burned.

keyTerms.meaning: It should be put away (stored or buried respectfully)
An informer who hands Jews over to the authorities
A Jew who has abandoned the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists. A scroll by a מין is burned (step 4). Here the גמרא only uses רב המנונא's list to show that a גוי's scroll is unfit and put away, not burned.

phrases.english: And that which is taught, 'it should be put away'
follows this תנא,
as רב המנונא taught,
the son of רבא from פשרוניא:
A ספר תורה, תפילין, and מזוזות
that were written by a heretic, or an informer,
a gentile, or a slave, a woman, or a minor,
or a כותי, or a Jewish apostate, are unfit;
as it is said: 'And you shall tie them' … 'and you shall write them'
Whoever is included in tying
is included in writing,
and whoever is not included in tying
is not included in writing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּתַנְיָא ״יִגָּנֵז״ – הַאי תַּנָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same answer, now explaining the second ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Put it away' follows רב המנונא's ברייתא: a גוי is not obligated in tying תפילין, so his writing is unfit.

steps.title: The 'read from it' ברייתא follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that allows reading from it follows a ברייתא that permits buying scrolls from גוים. In that ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allowed buying from a גוי scribe in צידן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא that says 'we may read from it' follows this תנא. A ברייתא teaches that we may buy scrolls from גוים anywhere, as long as they are written properly. There was once a גוי in צידן who wrote scrolls, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allowed people to buy from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third ברייתא, 'read from it.' It brings a source showing a תנא who allows using a scroll written by a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This תנא only requires that the scroll be written correctly. Who wrote it does not matter to him. The story about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל shows he allowed buying, and so using, scrolls a גוי wrote.
steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions about a scroll written by a גוי: רבי אליעזר says burn it, רב המנונא's ברייתא says put it away, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows reading from it.

phrases.english: And that which is taught, 'we may read from it'
follows this תנא, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: לוֹקְחִין סְפָרִים מִן הַגּוֹיִם בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: We may buy scrolls from gentiles in any place,
as long as they are written according to their laws.
And there was an incident with a certain gentile in צידן
who used to write scrolls,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִתִּיר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לִיקַּח מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל permitted buying from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּתַנְיָא ״קוֹרִין בּוֹ״ – הַאי תַּנָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer by explaining the third ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Read from it' follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allowed buying scrolls written by a גוי.

steps.title: Does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל require the processing but not the writing to be for the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. If he requires the parchment to be processed for the מצוה, he should surely require the writing to be for the מצוה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל require the processing of the parchment to be for the מצוה, yet not require the writing to be for the מצוה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave for the third ברייתא. It points out a problem with saying רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a scroll written by a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Processing the parchment is only a preparation, and writing is the main act. If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is strict about the preparation being לשמה, he should be even stricter about the writing. A גוי does not write לשמה, so how could he allow the scroll?

keyTerms.meaning: For their sake, meaning for the מצוה

phrases.english: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל:
does he require processing for their sake,
but not require writing for their sake?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל – עִיבּוּד לִשְׁמָן בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution of 'read from it' to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a scroll written by a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Writing matters more than processing. If he requires processing לשמה, he must require writing לשמה, and a גוי's writing is not לשמה.

steps.title: The source that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires processing for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about patching תפילין shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires the leather to be processed for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone coated תפילין with gold, or patched them with skin from a non-kosher animal, they are unfit. If he patched them with skin from a kosher animal, they are fit, even though he did not process the skin for the מצוה‎. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even with kosher skin they are unfit until he processes it for the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim in Step 9 that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires parchment processed for the מצוה. This backs up the challenge against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows a kosher-animal patch even if it was not processed for the מצוה‎. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it must be processed for the מצוה. If even the processing must be for the מצוה, then surely the writing must be too. So how could he allow buying scrolls written by a גוי in צידן?

keyTerms.meaning: processed the leather for the sake of the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא does not answer the question from Step 9. It proves the premise of that question: that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל really does require processing for the מצוה.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
If he coated them with gold
phrases.notes: "Them" means תפילין. The ברייתא is about the leather boxes.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁטָּלָה עֲלֵיהֶן עוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה –
phrases.english: or patched them with the skin of a non-kosher animal –
they are unfit.
With the skin of a kosher animal – they are fit,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא עִיבְּדָן לִשְׁמָן.
phrases.english: even though he did not process them for their sake.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even with the skin of a kosher animal – they are unfit,
until he processes them for their sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the premise of the challenge in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires parchment or leather processed for the מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about patching תפילין with kosher-animal skin.

steps.title: The scribe in צידן was a גר who went back to his old ways
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל answers that the scribe in צידן was not really a גוי. He was a convert who went back to living like a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל said: It was a convert who went back to his old ways.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל answers the challenge against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The scribe in צידן was actually a Jew, a גר who slipped back into his old lifestyle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a גר stays Jewish even if he goes back to his old ways, his writing counts as a Jew's writing. So רבן שמעון בן גמליאל never allowed writing by a real גוי. That keeps him consistent with his own strict view on processing for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: went back to his old (bad) ways

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel said:
It is about a convert who returned to his old ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּגֵר שֶׁחָזַר לְסוֹרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in Steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the scribe was a Jewish convert, not a real גוי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allowed scrolls written by a real גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The scribe was a Jew (a lapsed גר), so the writing counts as done by a Jew.

steps.title: Someone who abandoned Judaism should be even worse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a convert who went back to his old ways is a מין, which is even worse than a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to his old ways?! All the more so, he is a heretic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר שמואל's answer. A Jew who abandons the Torah is a מין, so his scrolls should be even more unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מין's writing is treated as worse than a גוי's. So calling the scribe a lapsed גר makes things worse, not better. The answer seems to backfire.

keyTerms.meaning: a heretic, a Jew who rejects the Torah

phrases.english: To his old ways?!
All the more so, since he is a heretic!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹרוֹ?! כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּהָוֵי לֵיהּ מִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר שמואל's claim that the scribe was a convert who returned to his old ways.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Jew who leaves the Torah is a מין, whose scrolls are even more unfit than a גוי's. So the answer makes the problem worse.

steps.title: He went back only out of fear
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the convert stopped acting Jewish only out of fear, not because he rejected the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He went back to his old ways out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי fixes רבה בר שמואל's answer. The convert stopped acting Jewish because he was afraid, so he is not a מין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מין rejects the Torah in his heart. This convert still believes but is scared to live openly as a Jew. So he is still a regular Jew, and the scrolls he writes may be read from.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling in צידן is about a Jewish convert who hid his Judaism out of fear. It is not about a real גוי, so it fits his strict view.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
That he returns to his old ways because of fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שֶׁחוֹזֵר לְסוֹרוֹ מִשּׁוּם יִרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 12 by narrowing the case of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: he lapsed out of fear, not out of belief.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A convert who went back to his old ways must be a מין.
steps.terutzMaskana: He went back only out of fear, so he is still a Jew and not a מין.

steps.title: One may pay slightly above value for holy items
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when buying holy items from a גוי, one may pay a bit more than their worth, up to a טרפעיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We may raise the price above their value, up to a טרפעיק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, connected to the משנה's rule that we don't buy holy items from גוים for more than their value. A ברייתא says a small extra amount is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids overpaying so that גוים are not encouraged to steal holy items. The ברייתא sets a small limit: up to a טרפעיק above value is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: we may raise the price above their value

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We may raise the price beyond their value,
up to a terapa'ik.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲלִין בִּדְמֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: how much one may pay a גוי for holy items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may pay up to a טרפעיק above value for holy items bought from a גוי.

steps.title: What is a טרפעיק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word טרפעיק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a טרפעיק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unusual word in the ברייתא. This sets up רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To use the rule, we need to know how much a טרפעיק is. So the גמרא asks for a definition.

phrases.english: What is a terapa'ik?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַרְפָּעִיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the ברייתא in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and amount of a טרפעיק.

steps.title: A טרפעיק is an איסתירא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that a טרפעיק is an איסתירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is an איסתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that a טרפעיק is the coin called an איסתירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives the ברייתא a clear amount: one may overpay by up to an איסתירא, a small coin.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: An istera.
phrases.notes: An איסתירא is a small coin, worth half a דינר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אִיסְתֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.

steps.title: אביי offers too little and the תפילין are thrown away
steps.stepSummary: An Arab merchant woman brings a sack of תפילין to אביי. He offers a date per pair, and she angrily throws them into the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain Arab merchant woman brought a sack of תפילין before אביי. He said to her: Will you give me each pair for a date? She was filled with anger, took them, and threw them into the river.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story connected to the rule about prices. אביי offers far too little for תפילין, and the seller angrily destroys them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי tried to avoid overpaying a גוי, in line with the משנה. But by offering almost nothing, he insulted her, and the holy items were lost.

phrases.english: A certain Arab merchant woman
who brought a sack of tefillin
before Abaye.
He said to her:
Will you give me each one for a date?
phrases.notes: Literally "head by head for dates." He means each pair for one date, a tiny price.

phrases.english: She was filled with anger,
took them, and threw them into the river.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא טַיַּיעְתָּא דְּאַיְיתַי חַיְיתָא דִתְפִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows the price rule of Step 14 in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offering far below value for holy items can lead to their destruction.

steps.title: אביי regrets insulting the תפילין
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he should not have belittled the תפילין so much in front of her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I should not have belittled them so much in front of her.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי reflects on what happened and admits he made a mistake by offering so little.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson is balance: don't overpay a גוי for holy items, but don't insult them with a tiny price either. Paying a fair price, even slightly above value, protects the holy items.
steps.whatToRemember: When buying holy items from a גוי, don't overpay, since a small extra up to an איסתירא is the limit. But don't belittle them with an insulting offer either.

phrases.english: He said:
I should not have belittled them
so much in front of her.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אִבְּעַי לִי לְזַלְזוֹלִינְהוּ בְּאַפַּהּ כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי's lesson from the story in Step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One must not insult holy items with a tiny offer. A fair price protects them from being destroyed.

steps.title: The new משנה: no remarrying after divorce for a bad reputation or a vow
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a man who divorces his wife because of a שם רע or because of a נדר may not remarry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: A man who divorces his wife because of a bad reputation may not take her back. If he divorces her because of a vow, he may not take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives two cases where a man who divorced his wife may never remarry her: a bad reputation, and a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a man may remarry his divorced wife. Here the משנה names two reasons for divorce that block remarriage forever. The משנה does not give the reason for this yet, and the גמרא will discuss it.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of the משנה text.
One who sends his wife out, meaning one who divorces her.
A bad reputation. Here it means a rumor that she was unfaithful.
He may not take her back (remarry her).

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not mean the bad reputation has to be true. It is talking about the reason he gave for divorcing her. Even if the rumor later turns out to be false, he still may not remarry her.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who divorces his wife
because of a bad reputation
may not take her back.
Because of a vow
he may not take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שֵׁם רַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new topic after the story of אביי and the תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who divorces his wife because of a שם רע or a נדר may not remarry her.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: it depends whether the public knew about the vow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה limits the vow rule. If many people knew of the vow, he may not remarry her. If not, he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: for any vow that many people knew about, he may not take her back. For a vow that many people did not know about, he may take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה narrows the vow case of the משנה. The ban only applies when the vow was publicly known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה forbade remarriage for every vow. רבי יהודה adds a dividing line: a public vow blocks remarriage, while a private vow does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Many people knew about it. The vow was public.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Any vow that many people knew about
he may not take her back,
and one that many people did not know about
he may take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל נֶדֶר שֶׁיָּדְעוּ בּוֹ רַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the vow case of the first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remarriage is forbidden only when the vow was known to the public.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: it depends whether the vow needs a חכם to cancel it
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a vow that needs a חכם to cancel it blocks remarriage, but a vow that does not need a חכם does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: for any vow that needs a sage's investigation, he may not take her back. For a vow that does not need a sage's investigation, he may take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a different dividing line for the vow case. It is not about whether the vow was public, but whether it needs a חכם to release it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some vows can only be released by a חכם, who looks into the case first. Other vows do not need that step. רבי מאיר says only the first kind blocks remarriage.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage's investigation. A חכם looks into the vow in order to release it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Any vow that needs a sage's investigation
he may not take her back,
and one that does not need a sage's investigation
he may take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל נֶדֶר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ חֲקִירַת חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different way from רבי יהודה's to limit the vow case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remarriage is forbidden only for a vow that needs a חכם to release it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: one case was forbidden only because of the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the ban in one vow case exists only because of the other vow case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: they only forbade this case because of that case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר comments on רבי מאיר's split. He says one of the two vow cases was forbidden only to protect the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר made remarriage depend on whether the vow needs a חכם. רבי אלעזר says the ban on one type of vow is not its own rule. It was made only because of the other type. The משנה does not say how this works, and the גמרא will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Except because of, only because of.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אָסְרוּ זֶה אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי זֶה.
phrases.english: They forbade this only because of that.
phrases.notes: The first 'this' is the vow that needs a חכם. The second 'that' is the vow that doesn't need one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא אָסְרוּ זֶה אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי מאיר's two vow cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on remarriage in the vow that needs a חכם exists only because of the vow that does not need one.

steps.title: The story in ציידן: the חכמים allowed him to take her back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reports that a man in ציידן vowed to divorce his wife and did so. The חכמים then allowed him to remarry her for the sake of תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: there was an incident in ציידן with a man who said to his wife, 'קונם if I do not divorce you.' He divorced her, and the sages allowed him to take her back, for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a true story. In this story the divorce happened because of a vow, yet the חכמים allowed the man to remarry his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here it was the husband himself who made the vow, forcing himself to divorce her. Even so, the חכמים permitted him to take her back. They said this was because of תיקון העולם.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow word. It means 'forbidden to me like a קרבן'.
The betterment of the world, a rabbinic reason for setting a rule.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three views on the vow case: the first opinion (every vow blocks remarriage), רבי יהודה (only a public vow), and רבי מאיר (only a vow that needs a חכם). It ends with a story where the חכמים allowed remarriage after a vow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said:
There was an incident in Tzaidan,
with one man who said to his wife:
'Konam if I do not divorce you,'
phrases.notes: He means: 'Everything should be forbidden to me like a קרבן if I don't divorce you.' He is forcing himself to divorce her.

phrases.english: and he divorced her,
and the sages permitted him to take her back,
for the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּצַיְדָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story where remarriage after a vow-based divorce was allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband vowed to divorce his wife, the חכמים allowed him to remarry her because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the rule applies only when he said his reason out loud
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. רב נחמן says the ban on remarriage applies only when the husband told his wife, 'I am divorcing you because of a bad reputation.'
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: this applies only when he said to her, 'I am divorcing you because of a bad reputation';
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by limiting the משנה's rule. The sentence ends with a semicolon, so the גמרא is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just divorcing her after a rumor is not enough to block remarriage. The husband must clearly tell her that the bad reputation is his reason. Only then does the משנה's ban apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא. It marks the start of the גמרא's discussion.
'And that is when', a phrase that adds a condition to a rule.
I am sending you out, meaning I am divorcing you.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key condition for the whole משנה. The ban depends on the reason being stated out loud, not just on what the husband was thinking.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said
that Rav Naḥman said:
This applies only when he said to her:
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's rule that he may not take her back.

phrases.english: 'I am divorcing you because of a bad reputation';

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: וְהוּא שֶׁאָמַר לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first line of the גמרא, limiting the משנה's rule about שם רע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on remarriage applies only if the husband told his wife outright that he was divorcing her because of a שם רע.
